title: Post-launch metrics readout + retro for Latency/$ Benchmark Report
creator: Talia Benson
description:
We shipped the public Latency/$ benchmark report + landing page. This ticket runs the post-launch readout and cross-functional retro.

Goals:
- Quantify launch impact (traffic → download → signup → meetings → pipeline)
- Validate that tracking/attribution is trustworthy (UTMs + HubSpot + product signups)
- Capture what worked / what didn’t across channels
- Make a recommendation for refresh cadence + what changes we should make before the next publication

Scope:
- KPI results vs pre-launch expectations (PM-418)
- Funnel performance (landing page, PDF downloads, API signups, demo requests)
- Pipeline influence (new opps and influenced opps; by segment/region)
- Support + SE feedback (common inbound questions; friction points)
- Recommendations (cadence, coverage, methodology changes, next assets)

Out of scope:
- Re-litigating the benchmark methodology (use the anomaly triage + methodology docs for deep dives)
- Publishing additional raw data externally
acceptance_criteria:
1) A 45-min post-launch readout is held with Marketing + Sales Ops + Perf/Evals + Support.
2) A written summary is posted (in this ticket) with: KPI table, funnel conversion rates, pipeline influence, and channel notes.
3) At least 5 concrete actions are captured with owners + target dates (follow-ups can become new tickets).
4) A recommendation is made on refresh cadence (and whether we keep the same workload definition) with explicit trade-offs.
5) Confirm tracking integrity: UTMs mapped to campaigns; report downloads reconciled across web analytics + form submissions; pipeline influence methodology stated.

2) Funnel conversion + attribution confidence (10m) — Tyler/Isabelle

Attendees: Camila Reyes, Ben Carter, Tyler Benson, Isabelle Laurent, Jordan Blake, Markus Klein, Dev Patel, Jasmine Liu, Jonas Weber (optional), Claire Dubois (optional)
kpi_scoreboard_summary:
Reporting window: Launch day (2025-02-24) through 2025-03-07 (first 12 business days)

Topline web KPIs (all regions)
- Landing page sessions: 182,430
- Report (PDF) downloads: 12,980
- Download conversion rate: 7.1%
- Avg time on page: 2m 41s
- Top entry channels: organic search (34%), paid social (22%), direct (18%), partner referrals (11%), email (9%), other (6%)

Product + Sales KPIs
- New Hosted API signups attributed to campaign UTMs: 1,240
- % of signups that made first inference call within 24h: 38%
- “Book a consult” / “Talk to us” form submissions: 310
- Sales meetings held (net-new) attributed to report: 96

Pipeline (HubSpot reporting; see notes in ‘attribution_integrity’)
- New pipeline created (net-new opps with first-touch = report campaign): $1.84M
- Influenced pipeline (existing opps with engagement on landing/download/email within window): $6.10M
- Highest-intent segments: Dedicated (throughput/cost buyers), EMEA data residency prospects, APAC-heavy apps asking about region coverage

Notes:
- Conversion is materially higher on email + partner traffic than on paid social; paid social drove volume but lower consult-intent.
- Field reports: prospects consistently asked for: (a) reproducibility steps, (b) region routing guidance, (c) variance/confidence intervals language.
funnel_details:
Funnel definition used for this readout
- Step 1: Landing page session
- Step 2: PDF download (form submit OR direct file download w/ event capture)
- Step 3: Signup (Hosted API)
- Step 4: Activation (first successful inference request)
- Step 5: Sales intent (meeting held OR consult form submit)

Observed conversion rates (window: 2025-02-24 → 2025-03-07)
- Session → download: 7.1%
- Download → signup: 9.6%
- Signup → activation (24h): 38%
- Download → meeting/consult: 2.1%

Breakdown notes
- EMEA sessions had a slightly lower download rate but higher meeting intent (more enterprise evaluation behavior).
- APAC sessions disproportionately clicked the region table + routing FAQ; highest exit rate was on the methodology appendix page (suggests we should add a short TL;DR at the top and keep the long form below).
pipeline_influence_methodology:
Methodology (Sales Ops)
- First-touch attribution: earliest tracked campaign interaction for a contact/company in the period; pipeline counted only if a new opportunity was created after that first-touch.
- Influenced pipeline: opportunity already existed, but at least one associated contact had a tracked interaction with the report campaign during the reporting window (landing page view, download, or nurture click).
- Exclusions: internal Redwood traffic; duplicates merged; contacts with missing UTM/referrer are not counted as first-touch (but can count as influenced if we have engagement events).

Caveats
- Some consult requests came via AE-forwarded email (no UTM) and are under-counted in first-touch.
- Marketplace/partner referrals are tracked, but co-marketing links were not consistent across all partner posts (we should standardize partner UTM templates next time).
support_and_field_feedback:
Support/CS themes (Dev/Jasmine)
- #1: “Why does my region latency not match the report?” → environment differences, routing policies, different sequence lengths/concurrency; need a short ‘checklist’ doc for customers.
- #2: “Are you using customer traffic/logs?” → clear ‘no customer-identifying traces’ answer worked; point to Security/Data Handling FAQ.
- #3: “Is the metric stable / can I reproduce it?” → customers want a minimal reproduction recipe + explicit variance bands.

SE/Field themes (Markus/Jordan)
- Competitive pushback was mostly about workload representativeness and variance.
- The ‘latency/$’ framing landed well with engineering + procurement, but only when we led with constraints (what it measures / what it doesn’t).
- Several enterprise accounts asked for Dedicated pricing tie-in; we need a tighter ‘how to estimate your unit cost’ worksheet (without turning the report into a price sheet).
retro_outcomes:
What worked
- Single primary metric (latency/$) made the story memorable; supporting metrics were enough for deeper buyers.
- Methodology appendix + confidence/variance language reduced credibility challenges in analyst conversations.
- Partner amplification drove high-quality traffic when the partner included a short ‘why this matters’ snippet (not just a link).

What didn’t
- Methodology appendix page is too dense at the top; we buried the ‘how to interpret’ section.
- Some inbound confusion between Hosted vs Dedicated results (people assumed tables were Dedicated-only). We need clearer labeling on the landing page and in the PDF.
- APAC interest was high; our APAC region coverage is still perceived as “new” and needed more upfront explanation (routing/fallback, data residency boundaries).

Risks discovered
- Attribution gaps from AE-forwarded links and a handful of missing UTMs on social variants.
- A few dashboards/screenshots used in internal validation were hard to locate quickly during analyst Q&A (need a single index page/kit).
refresh_cadence_recommendation:
Recommendation: Quarterly refresh (every ~12 weeks), with a strict change log and ‘comparability mode’.

Rationale
- Model + kernel/runtime updates materially change inference economics; a quarterly refresh stays credible without turning this into a continuous ops burden.
- Monthly is too noisy (variance + capacity windows + constant narrative churn).

Guardrails
- Keep the workload definition stable for at least 2 quarters; if we change it, publish a clear ‘v2 methodology’ label and do not compare directly to prior numbers.
- Publish a versioned table (e.g., 2025Q1, 2025Q2) and keep prior versions accessible.
- Schedule capacity windows in advance; avoid running benchmarks during known high-traffic periods.

Next-iteration scope suggestions
- Add a short ‘How to use this report’ section at the very top (1 page) with 3–5 bullets.
- Expand APAC region coverage and call it out explicitly.
- Add one reliability signal (e.g., error rate under load during benchmark windows) only if we can define it cleanly without over-claiming.
